text:
eva: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of ~18-25% 503s hitting hosted inference since 12:12 UTC. Multiple customers (AcmeProd noted) report large timeouts then 503s. Root cause looks upstream (worker restarts). Any oncall?

gina: I'm on it, pulling logs for the prod-gpu pools now.

frank: quick summary from node logs: repeated container restarts on pool prod-gpu-4 across nodes az1/az2. Saw SIGSEGV in the attention kernel, and intermittent 'CUDA out of memory' during KV prefetch. Paste of recent journal snippet:

```
Mar 18 12:13:01 prod-gpu-4-12 infer-runner[22345]: ERROR: worker 22345 exited with signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
Mar 18 12:13:01 prod-gpu-4-12 infer-runner[22345]: backtrace: 0x7f8abce... at attention.cu:line 1024
Mar 18 12:13:02 prod-gpu-4-12 nvidia: Out of memory allocating 256MB for kv_cache_prefetch
Mar 18 12:13:02 prod-gpu-4-12 systemd: infer-runner.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=11/SEGV
Mar 18 12:13:05 prod-gpu-4-12 systemd: infer-runner.service: Failed with result 'signal'
```

infra-bot: container prod-gpu-4-12/infer-runner restarted by k8s (BackOff) x3 within 60s.

ryan: I cross-checked API gateway logs — majority are 503 upstream errors; a small fraction are 401s but unrelated. The 503s correlate with the worker restart windows (12:12:58 -> 12:14:10).

cs-lead: CS on call with Acme now, they're seeing 10s+ latencies then 503s. They want ETA and workaround ASAP.

eva: Can we apply an immediate mitigation? In prior incidents disabling KV-prefetch for large contexts cut OOM risk. If we can flip that flag for the affected model group for a canary subset, might stop the coredumps.

frank: Agree. I'm preparing a canary change: MODEL_X_PREFETCH=false on 2 nodes in prod-gpu-4 pool. Also propose lowering dynamic batch max tokens from 4096 -> 2048 to reduce memory pressure.

frank: Pushing canary now:

```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/infer-runner MODEL_X_PREFETCH=false --record
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/infer-runner --selector=pool=prod-gpu-4 --max-unavailable=1
```

deploy-bot: Rollout started for infer-runner in namespace infra (selector pool=prod-gpu-4). Canary nodes: prod-gpu-4-12, prod-gpu-4-13.

gina: Adding temporary routing policy: requests with context length > 32k tokens will be routed to fallback smaller model (redwood-slim) and queued. This reduces pressure until we confirm canary.

ryan: Repro notes for infra: to reproduce locally -> send concurrent toolcalls with large context + prefetch enabled. Example:

```
# repro load (replace HOST and API_KEY)
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"MODEL_X","input":"<32k token payload>","prefetch":true,"max_tokens":1024}' &
done
```

frank: Observed behavior when reproducing: after ~30-45s sustained QPS at target, memory climbs and OOM occurs during kv prefetch stage; then segfault in attention kernel.

cs-lead: Please confirm if there's a short-term customer-facing workaround we can give Acme. They asked if reducing request size or toggling `prefetch:false` client-side helps.

eva: Yes — advise them to set prefetch:false and cap context length to <= 16k tokens. Also ask them to reduce concurrency temporarily. We'll push server-side mitigations too.

gina: Canary finished initial validation: 2 nodes with MODEL_X_PREFETCH=false held stable for 6 minutes under limited synthetic load. No restarts observed on those canary pods.

frank: Rolling to 30% of prod-gpu-4 pool now. If no regressions in 10m, roll to 100% and restore batching thresholds to sane defaults. If restarts persist, fallback is to revert to older quantized runtime (which has shown stability) or enable dedicated fallback routing (move customers to dedicated capacity).

deploy-bot: Rollout to 30% started; target pods: prod-gpu-4-11..14.

gina: Alerts created/updated: set incident alert if 503 rate > 5% for 5m and host restart count > 2 in 1m. Also added a dashboard panel for KV cache mem growth.

ryan: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem to analyze attention kernel traces and compile flags; 2) include a throttling rule in gateway for oversized toolcalls; 3) test hotfix driver/attention kernel on CI.

cs-lead: I told Acme support team the temporary workaround (prefetch:false + reduce context/concurrency) and that we're rolling a server-side mitigation now. They asked for ETA — told them 30m for initial rollback/mitigations and will update.

eva: Thanks. Once canary hits 30% and we confirm stability, I'll send a short CS update and a recommended client-side config snippet.

frank: If you need the kernel backtrace or heap dumps I uploaded them to /artifacts/incident-8512340000/ — attaching short snippet here for the trace team:

```
# short backtrace
#0  0x7f8abced in attention_kernel
#1  0x7f8abf1d in compute_attention
#2  0x7f8ac001 in model_forward
#3  0x55b1a2 in runner_loop
```

gina: Good work team. Marking as active incident; will update in 10m. @cs-lead ping if customer wants deeper context. :thumbsup:

cs-lead: Thanks — Acme acknowledged workaround, will hold off until 30m update.

eva: Plan documented in incident tracker (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1729).
